newsitem.title: BOTSWANA: Botswana told to speed up economic diversification.
newsitem.headline: Botswana told to speed up economic diversification.

text.p: Rapid growth in Botswana's gross domestic product (GDP) during fiscal 1995/96 (July-June) was largely in mining and the continued rapid expansion of the government sector, the Bank of Botswana said in its annual economic review for 1996.
"To achieve its development goals and objectives, Botswana must resolve some of the most critical issues it has ever faced," the Bank said.
In spite of policies directed at diversification of the economy, non-mining GDP grew by only 0.1 percent above that recorded for 1994/95.
Rapid growth in the labour force growth had led to high unemployment, widespread poverty and economic deprivation.

"The need for job creation is even more pressing than ever. Although the formal sector has grown rapidly and employs an estimated 45 percent of the labour force, the informal sector does not have the capacity to provide jobs for the rest," the review aid.
Estimates of overall unemployment for the year to September 1996 were 21.3 percent.

It would not be possible to rely on government-led growth to create enough jobs to absorb those entering the labour market. Nor would the mining sector - even if it continued to expand rapidly - do much to reduce unemployment. Diamond mining in particlar was highly capital intensive.

"If the unemployment problem is to be solved, economic diversification is necessary and this requires a much more prominent role for the private sector. Macroeconomic stability, and the policies which promote it, will have to encompass this requirement," the Bank said.
Real overall growth of 7.0 percent was the highest since 1990/91 against the previous year's 3.1 percent. Non-mining GDP grew by 5.6 percent.
